Subject: Final interview debrief: Alex Mateo (SWE IC4) — score synthesis & owner

Hi all,

Thanks again for taking the time to interview Alex yesterday. I've attached the panel scorecard and the take-home assignment results. We need to close the loop on scoring and decide who will own the final synthesis that's sent to recruiting.

Ask: please add (1) your final numeric scores in the scorecard (0-5 per rubric) and (2) a one-line justification for any score 3 or below. If you have a short note about signal/concern that matters for calibration, paste it inline.

Timing: aiming to ship a consolidated recommendation to Sara by EOD today (PST). If you can't make EOD, flag your ETA here.

Initial thought: if we still have a tie on overall recommended hire decision, I'd propose Jonas take the tiebreak (he's deepest on the infra story). If anyone objects to that role, speak now.

Attachments: alex_mateo_resume.pdf (resume), alex_assignment_results.xlsx (assignment + grader notes), panel_scorecard-aggregated.csv (empty; please populate)

Drive: https://drive.re/redwood/hiring/alex-mateo/debrief
HubSpot: hubspot:deal_83421

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

> Thanks again for taking the time to interview Alex yesterday. I've attached the panel scorecard and the take-home assignment results. We need to close the loop on scoring and decide who will own the final synthesis that's sent to recruiting.

Done — I updated the scorecard with my numbers and a short note. Quick summary inline:
- System design: 4 (good trade-offs; wanted clearer fault-isolation plan)
- Code/implementation thoughtfulness: 4
- Culture/ownership: 5
- Communication: 4

Main strength: pragmatic trade-offs and clear prioritization on shipping.
Main concern: limited exposure to clustered KV internals at scale (we should test for that in the final loop if we move forward).

If we need a tie-break, I'm fine owning it as Neha suggested.

—Jonas
Senior Staff SWE

I've added my scores too and uploaded a short matrix of gaps (see panel_scorecard-aggregated.csv). High level:
- Overall leaning: Hire (strong product sense + ship bias)
- Outlier: system-design depth — two interviewers called this 'good but not deep' which shows up in the variance column.

Proposal: Tessa to stitch the one-line justifications into the final paragraph and propose either an offer or a targeted final technical check (one-hour deep dive with Jonas) depending on how Tessa reads the spread.

I'm available for a quick 3:00 PM PST sync if it's helpful. If we don't sync, please still update the scorecard by 4:30 so Sara can start reference work.

Thanks everyone — good sync.

Tessa: please own the synthesis. Action items:
1) Consolidate the numeric scores + one-line justifications into the final recommendation paragraph. Use the drive file as the source of truth.
2) If the spread still looks ambiguous after you stitch notes, schedule a 30-minute tiebreak with Jonas and me (I'm available 4:30–5:30 PST).
3) If you recommend hire, trigger Sara to begin reference checks and prepare the standard offer channel. If you recommend a targeted final check, note the scope for Jonas to lead.

Sara: please stand by to open references once Tessa confirms and to shepherd the candidate timeline; tentatively aim for references to start Monday morning.

I'll send the final note to recruiting once Tessa confirms (please try to close by EOD PST). Thanks for the quick turn-around.
